h: Vayetzei Ois 4 · Yaakov's Departure: Glory, Radiance and Splendor of the Tzaddik
Why the Torah Records Yaakov's Departure

p: "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva
"Did no one else leave from there
When the tzaddik is in the city,
he is its radiance, he is its splendor;
'And she went out from the place,' etc.
for there was no one there
where Yitzchak and Rivkah were present, etc.?
That is, what troubled [the Midrash] was:
why is "And he went out" written?
From this [we see] that his departure
was a matter in its own right,
as is written in Rashi's commentary.
to Avimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar,"
and his departure from the place is not mentioned.
And there all the more it should have
mentioned his departure from the place,
that its glory departed, its radiance departed,
for there there did not remain
any tzaddik at all in his place,
where Yitzchak and Rivkah were present,
only that "it is not comparable, etc."
And why is the departure mentioned

While the tzaddik is in a city he is its radiance and splendor; when he leaves, they depart. With Naomi (Ruth 1:7) that is understandable, since she was the only righteous one there, but Yitzchak and Rivkah remained in Be'er Sheva — and the answer: the merit of one tzaddik is not like the merit of two. rich.text: (Rav Tzadok) — reads the same Midrash (ויצא יעקב וכי לא יצא משם אלא הוא … ניחא דתמן לא היתה אלא אותה הצדקת בלבד אלא הכא דהוה יצחק ורבקה) and asks why the Midrash held back its question until after Naomi. His answer: Yaakov alone was called ziv, the light of the world (the “sun”), while Yitzchak became part of that radiance only once he too was called Yisrael. It adds the month of Iyar (ירח זיו), ziv as the Vav, the middle bar running from Keser to Malchus, and Yaakov as the image of Adam before the sin.

h: Yaakov and the Beauty of Adam

p: for the same reason that it is not said of the Avos
that they were the beauty of Adam HaRishon,
as it is stated in the Gemara
that he was a semblance of the beauty of Adam HaRishon,
(חֵלֶק ב, קיא סוֹף עַמּוּד א, וּבִשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
that he was the beauty and the image
And why is this not said
repaired the corruption of the serpent?
For it is stated in the Midrash Rabbah
הֲרֵי אֲנִי בּוֹרֵא אֶת הָאָדָם תְּחִלָּה
Avraham will come and repair in his stead."
And so it is stated in the holy Zohar
that Avraham said to Adam HaRishon:
אֲנָא זְמִין קַמֵּי קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
"I stand ready before the Holy One, blessed be He,
on your behalf, so that you shall never be ashamed"
Likewise Yitzchak our father, peace be upon him,
repaired the corruption of the serpent;
Only Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
"Would not even the lowest of the low
Rather, [he said it] in order to beget offspring, etc."
That is, he knew nothing at all
only a heart [set] on bringing forth flesh [offspring]
as it will be in the future
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם קלז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
(as written in the Midrash HaNe'elam, 137b, bottom);
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא עָלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ
and therefore it did not occur to him
that there is any shame in this,
of whom it is written, "and they were not ashamed."
And so it is stated in the Gemara
the contamination did not cease from our forefathers, etc."
And even according to the one who says
that refers only to his offspring,
from whom it ceased at the giving of the Torah,
that these and those are both the words of the living God.
But Yaakov, from his own side,
was like Adam HaRishon before the corruption;
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בַּגְּמָרָא וּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה
therefore it is said in the Gemara and Midrash Rabbah
like the beauty of Adam HaRishon,
and in the holy Zohar that he was
the very beauty of Adam HaRishon,
and he is the likeness of a man

p: "When the tzaddik is in the city,
he is its glory, he is its radiance,
And all three are likewise mentioned
"Hashem my God, You are very great;
You have clothed Yourself in glory and splendor."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה
This rests on what is written in the Midrash Rabbah
יִשְׂרָאֵל מְעַטְּרִין אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
"Israel crowns the Holy One, blessed be He,
that Hashem, may He be blessed, emanated
for the creation of the world,
a King clothed in ten garments.
refers to Keser Elyon (the Supernal Crown),
for this is what is called "great,"
for otherwise it is not great
except relative to what is smaller than it,
to Hashem, may He be blessed.
and this is the attribute of Ein Sof.
And it is written, "You have clothed Yourself in glory and splendor":
these are the first two garments.
Hod (glory) corresponds to the attribute of Keser Elyon,
that they tied two crowns on each of Israel
at the giving of the Torah, etc.,
and Moshe merited them all and took them;
the skin of his face shone."
And with Moshe they are called "rays of glory,"
as is written in Midrash Tanchuma
And the garment of hadar (splendor) corresponds to Chochmah.

h: Ziv as Binah: The Radiance in the Middle

p: for ziv (radiance) is the name for
what shines forth from Keser Elyon.
This is an expression we find in the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א, סד עַמּוּד א)
"and they delight in the radiance of the Shechinah."
וְכֵן בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קלה עַמּוּד ב)
So too in the holy Zohar (I 135b):
It is what shines forth from
to the Heh, which is the attribute of Malchus;
these are called Male and Female.
Likewise what shines forth from Chochmah to Binah,
which are called in the holy Zohar
and this is why they said "he is its radiance."
And "its radiance" is placed here in the middle —
הוּא הוֹדָהּ הוּא זִיוָהּ הוּא הֲדָרָהּ
"he is its glory, he is its radiance, he is its splendor" —
and is the inwardness of Keser,
[light] shines from Keser Elyon to Chochmah and Binah
through the tip of the Yud.
which is understanding one thing from another,

therefore there are mentioned with him
three expressions, "its glory, its radiance, its splendor,"
corresponding to the first three garments.

h: Why Yaakov's Leaving, Though Yitzchak Remained

p: and of Yitzchak it is written, "and I ate of all,"
that the evil inclination had no dominion over them,
and He gave him a taste of the World to Come —
that he was refined down to the root,
וְלֹא נִתְבָּרֵר עַד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and he was not refined until Yaakov our father, peace be upon him —
when indeed Yitzchak too was refined,
the essence of completeness was refined
Therefore it is written of Yaakov,
for its glory, radiance and splendor departed.
And this is what is said in the Midrash Rabbah:
לֹא דּוֹמֶה זְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק אֶחָד
"The merit of one tzaddik is not comparable
to the merit of two tzaddikim."
Although we said that this matter
of "its glory, its radiance, its splendor"
הָיָה נִכָּר גַּם הַזִּיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק
the radiance of Yitzchak too was discernible,
and that he was refined in all the attributes,
for she brought Ruth under the wings of the Shechinah,
in whom the soul of Mashiach was contained,
and repair the entire blemish of the serpent.
And of Mashiach it is expounded
it is written, "And she went out,"
for its glory, radiance and splendor departed,
alluding to the first three attributes, as stated.

h: The Third Meal: Beholding the Radiance

p: which corresponds to Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
when the Shabbat has already passed in [proper] observance,
so that one merits the holiness of the Avos,
who are branches of the first three,
we say, "to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin."
"To behold" means recognition in the heart,
"And my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
That is the radiance that shines into the heart:
Likewise the last attribute is called heart,
means when the fear [of Heaven] enters
as it says, "and his heart will understand, and he will return."
This is Imma Ila'ah (the Supernal Mother),
and this attribute is called ziv
on account of the shining and illumination
And this is "to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּאִדְּרָא רַבָּא
according to what is written in the Idra Rabba
"The face of the Ancient of Days shines
into the face of Ze'ir Anpin, etc.,
and then it is called a time of favor"
And then the completeness of the radiance
and illumination in the heart is discerned.

rich.text: (Rav Tzadok) — opens with the same line, בני היכלא דכסיפין למיחזי זיו דזעיר אנפין, and explains that the ziv can be seen דייקא בסעודה זו לאחר שפנה כל יום השבת בקדושה — only at the third meal, once the whole Shabbat has passed in holiness (as here: וּכְבָר עָבַר הַשַּׁבָּת בִּשְׁמִירָה). It identifies that radiance with שופריה דיעקב מעין שופריה דאדה״ר and adds the Midrash that Adam kept his radiance through the first Shabbat.
